title: McDonald's hit with class action alleging AI-powered menu price-fixing
source_used: Reuters wire text as carried by The Economic Times (Reuters page itself returns 401); cross-checked with PYMNTS, National Technology News, Livemint and Law Commentary
key_facts: McDonald's was sued in federal court in Chicago in a proposed nationwide class action alleging it illegally coordinates menu prices across its franchises and company-owned restaurants through an AI-powered pricing system.

The lawsuit, filed on Friday (2 Oct 2026), says McDonald's violated US antitrust law by conspiring with independent franchisees to fix prices using algorithms trained on nonpublic data; it states 'Independent businesses must set their prices independently'.

Reuters reported last week (29 Sep) that McDonald's pricing engine uses machine-learning algorithms to continually analyze data from millions of daily transactions across its nearly 14,000 restaurants; the lawsuit cites that article, which said other fast-food companies are also turning to AI for pricing.

McDonald's, in a statement on Monday (5 Oct), called the allegations speculative and uninformed: 'AI does not set the price of a Big Mac or any other menu item'; it said franchisees make their own pricing decisions and that pricing recommendation tools and analytics are widespread across industries.

The plaintiff, an Illinois resident, seeks to represent a class of potentially millions of McDonald's customers; plaintiff's lawyer Lark Turner said McDonald's is 'leveraging its troves of data and its franchised system to nickel-and-dime consumers down to the last French fry'.
US plaintiffs have filed a wave of class actions in recent years alleging companies used algorithms or AI to illegally coordinate prices for hotel rooms, apartment rentals and other purchases.

why_it_matters_hint: A nationwide antitrust suit could test whether shared AI pricing recommendations across franchise restaurants amount to illegal price coordination; the claims are unproven and denied.
event_date: Lawsuit filed Fri 2 Oct 2026; reported and answered by McDonald's on Mon 5 Oct 2026; follows the Reuters investigation of 29 Sep 2026
notes: Reuters page returns 401, so read as the Reuters wire text on The Economic Times; PYMNTS, National Technology News, Livemint and Law Commentary agree and add: plaintiff Michael Thomas, filed 2 Oct in the Northern District of Illinois under Section 1 of the Sherman Act, alleges the system has run since at least 2019, and seeks damages and a court order. The case is only a proposed class action; the class has not been certified. Follow-up of 1005:C14-09 (Futurism relaying the Reuters investigation, entry 112 of our 5 Oct edition).
